newsitem.title: USA: NCC launches online price data for cotton growers.
newsitem.headline: NCC launches online price data for cotton growers.

text.p: In an attempt to make changing cotton prices and marketing information more accessible to farmers, the National Cotton Council (NCC) will launch a risk management program through the Internet, beginning in January.
Members who have access to the Cotton Risk Management Network can look up spot and mill-delivered prices, world price data, historic price data, the marketing loan rate, and NYCE options information.
Additionally, a farm model will allow users to evaluate cropping alternatives among cotton, wheat, soybeans and corn.

The first stage of the model will help growers identify the best crop for each field, based on economics. Eventually, the program will select the best crop and the number of acres devoted to each crop based on price expectations, production costs, and yields, Kevin Brinkley, the project manager and an economist with NCC, said.
"The bottom line is that farmers will have to get more involved in marketing than they have been in the past due to the Farm Act," Brinkley said.
The Federal Agriculture Improvement and Reform Act of 1996 reduces the government's role in underwriting price risk.

Software for the network will be available at NCC's annual Beltwide Cotton Conferences, held Jan 8 - 12 in New Orleans. The network can be accessed at NCC's World Wide Web home page (http://www.cotton.org).
Brinkley said between 2,000 and 3,000 members will use the network in its first year, and 10,000 members after about three years. The network is free to NCC members.
